title: Theo and the Static
premise: Isandro Marchetti smuggles stolen memories through orbital customs around Meridian, a dying colony the Core has written off, recording its slow suffocation in contraband archives. When the deep-space ship Vantablack returns with a crew aged backward and carrying a message from an enemy that supposedly never existed, customs flags Isandro's own archived memories as evidence of treason. To survive, she must smuggle the message itself — hidden inside her own mind — past the blockade before the jump window closes, knowing delivery will either end the war with the Meridian separatists or ignite it. She delivers it, at the cost of the memories that made her who she was, and Meridian lives on in the archives of strangers.
about_author: Odile Ishikawa is a former radio archivist who spent six years cataloguing oral histories from decommissioned space stations before turning to fiction. She writes from a floating studio off the coast of Hokkaido, where she claims the static between stations sounds like memory.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Isandro runs a shipment of illegal memories past Meridian orbital customs, hiding them in the neural lattice of a dead man's prosthetic. Through her POV we see the colony's decay and her cynical professionalism. Beat: competence masking grief — she is archiving a world no one will buy.

chapters.title: The Dying Ledger
chapters.summary: Isandro visits the undercity archive where she records Meridian's slow death: water rationing, the Core's silent embargo. POV shifts to her client, old archivist Bem Osei, who begs her to smuggle out the colony's full memory record. Beat: the weight of being the only witness.

chapters.title: Something Comes Back
chapters.summary: The Vantablack, lost eleven years in deep space, appears at the jump gate — its crew biologically younger than when they left. Isandro watches from the docks as customs seizes the ship. Beat: wonder curdling into dread as the returned crew cannot remember the war.

chapters.title: Aged Backward
chapters.summary: Isandro is hired to fence a memory chip recovered from the Vantablack and discovers it contains her own face — a version of her she never lived. POV alternates with customs officer Dae Hyun-Woo, who suspects the ship is a weapon. Beat: uncanny vertigo, identity cracking.

chapters.title: The Message in the Hold
chapters.summary: The Vantablack's young captain, Sol Ferreira, reveals the ship carries a negotiated peace message from the separatist fleet — proof the war's first strike came from the Core. Customs has sealed the hold. Beat: Isandro realizes the message is the most valuable contraband in the system.

chapters.title: Customs House Ghosts
chapters.summary: Dae interrogates Isandro over anomalies in her archived memories, playing back recordings of events she has no recollection of living. Beat: horror — someone has been editing her, and the edits predate her smuggling career.

chapters.title: What the Static Remembers
chapters.summary: Isandro traces the tampering to Bem Osei's old archive rig and finds a hidden track: her childhood on Meridian, before the war, before she erased it. Beat: grief for a self she chose to amputate to survive the siege.

chapters.title: The Price Already Paid
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Isandro survives the Core's first bombardment by selling her own traumatic memories to a Core black-site, buying passage and silence. Beat: understanding that her entire identity is itself smuggled goods.

chapters.title: Two Isandros
chapters.summary: The Vantablack's memory bank contains a complete Isandro — pre-erasure, whole — recorded by the ship's deep-space archive before the war. Sol offers it to her. Beat: temptation of becoming whole versus the safety of who she has learned to be.

chapters.title: Sealed Hold, Sealed Throats
chapters.summary: Customs arrests Sol and impounds the message; the Core fleet announces it will board the Vantablack at the jump window. Dae, doubting his own orders, quietly returns Isandro's confiscated chips. Beat: an enemy becoming an ally in the dark.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Isandro plans the impossible: the message must be carried in a living mind to pass the Core's dead-man scanners, and hers is the only brain with the lattice scarring to hide it. Beat: cold calculation over terror — she volunteers to be the container.

chapters.title: Loading the Ghost
chapters.summary: In a stolen clinic, the peace message is spliced into Isandro's memory lattice alongside the recovered track of her erased self. The two records entangle. Beat: disorientation and strange peace — she can no longer tell which memories are hers, and stops wanting to.

chapters.title: Dae's Defection
chapters.summary: Dae falsifies the boarding manifest to get Isandro dockside access but is caught by his superior, Inspector Voss, who offers him a choice: betray her or be erased like the colony. Beat: Dae chooses the colony, burning his career.

chapters.title: Bem's Last Archive
chapters.summary: Bem Osei is killed in a Core raid on the undercity archive; Isandro reaches the wreckage in time to receive his final recording — the complete memory of Meridian, entrusted to her. Beat: the witness's burden doubles; she now carries a world and a peace treaty.

chapters.title: Running the Window
chapters.summary: Isandro and Dae steal a customs cutter and make for the jump gate as the Core fleet deploys. A running battle through the orbital debris field. Beat: kinetic escalation — the colony's own junk becomes their cover.

chapters.title: Voss at the Gate
chapters.summary: Inspector Voss corners them at the jump gate and offers Isandro her erased memories back — the original, unedited record — if she surrenders the message. Beat: the cruelest price: wholeness in exchange for Meridian's death warrant.

chapters.title: The Choice of Who Survives
chapters.summary: Isandro refuses; Dae sacrifices the cutter to disable the gate's Core lockdown, buying her minutes. Voss's strike team closes in. Beat: climax of loyalty — she runs, carrying everyone's memories but her own chance at peace.

chapters.title: Through the Static
chapters.summary: Isandro threads the jump gate under fire, the message and her fractured selves screaming in her lattice. The Core fleet fires on the gate as she jumps. Beat: transcendence through pain — the static between memories becomes a single signal.

chapters.title: Delivery
chapters.summary: She reaches the separatist fleet and delivers the message: proof of the Core's first strike, plus Bem's archive of Meridian's suffering. The fleet stands down and broadcasts both records system-wide. Beat: catharsis — the war ends not with a weapon but with testimony.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: The dead-man protocol triggers: delivering the message purged the entangled records, including the restored Isandro. She wakes with gaps she can name but not feel. Beat: quiet devastation — survival's invoice, finally presented.

chapters.title: The Colony That Remembers Itself
chapters.summary: Isandro returns to a Meridian no longer embargoed; the broadcast archive has made every citizen a witness. Dae, stripped of rank, meets her at the docks. Beat: bittersweet homecoming — the colony is saved, and she is a stranger in her own memory of it.

chapters.title: Static, Becoming Signal
chapters.summary: In the rebuilt undercity archive, Isandro records a new memory — her own, unedited, of everything that happened — and files it beside Bem's. She begins again as a smuggler of one thing only: true records. Beat: resolution — identity as something made, not recovered.
